task_1.title: Support coordinate-aware curvefit guesses, bounds, and optional fit error suppression
task_1.description: The curve fitting API now accepts coordinate-aligned DataArray values for initial guesses and parameter bounds so different slices can be fit with different starting conditions or constraints in one call. The update also adds an option to ignore optimization failures and return NaN coefficients and covariance for failed slices instead of aborting the full operation.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `DataArray.curvefit()` and `Dataset.curvefit()` can fit multidimensional data using per-slice initial guesses and bounds, and allow callers to choose whether optimization failures should raise or be surfaced as missing fit results.

expectation.grounded: `DataArray.curvefit()` and `Dataset.curvefit()` should accept `p0` entries as scalars or `DataArray` objects, and `bounds` entries as `(lower, upper)` pairs where either bound may be a scalar or `DataArray`. Array-valued guesses and bounds must broadcast over preserved data dimensions so each coordinate slice can receive different parameter initialization or limits. The `errors` argument should support `"raise"` and `"ignore"`: `"raise"` propagates fitting failures from SciPy, while `"ignore"` returns `NaN` values in `curvefit_coefficients` and covariance outputs for failed slices.
expectation.conceptual: Curve fitting should let users provide different starting guesses and parameter limits for different coordinate locations in a single call, rather than requiring manual loops. Users should also be able to opt into tolerant fitting so unsuccessful slices produce missing results instead of failing the entire fitting job.

constraints.grounded: Any `DataArray` provided in `p0` or `bounds` must only use dimensions that belong to the non-reduced dimensions preserved in the fit result; extra unrelated dimensions should be rejected with `ValueError`. The `errors` option must reject unsupported values with `ValueError`. Existing scalar `p0` and scalar bound behavior must remain valid, including mixed scalar/array bound pairs and default parameter initialization when values are omitted.
constraints.conceptual: The new flexibility must not silently accept misaligned array inputs or invalid mode values. Existing single-value guesses and bounds should continue to work unchanged, and partial failures should only be tolerated when the caller explicitly asks for that behavior.

behavior: Array-valued initial guesses can vary by preserved coordinates, and those values influence each slice's fitted parameter solution independently.
Array-valued lower and upper bounds can vary by preserved coordinates, including cases where one side is scalar and the other side is coordinate-dependent.
When default parameter values fall outside supplied bounds, feasible initial values are derived per slice using the provided bounds.
If a guess or bound `DataArray` includes dimensions outside the fitted data's preserved dimensions, `curvefit` raises `ValueError` before fitting.
When `errors="raise"`, optimization failures still raise the underlying runtime failure.
When `errors="ignore"`, failed fits yield `NaN` coefficients and covariance for the affected slices while successful slices remain available.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller provides `p0` as coordinate-aligned `DataArray` values for one or more parameters, `curvefit` should complete and use those per-slice guesses to produce slice-specific fitted coefficients.

When a caller provides `bounds` as scalar values, `DataArray` values, or a mix of both in `(lower, upper)` tuples, `curvefit` should apply those limits independently for each preserved coordinate slice.
When a `p0` or `bounds` `DataArray` contains a dimension that is not part of the preserved output dimensions, `curvefit` should fail with `ValueError` instead of attempting an implicit alignment.
When the caller omits some parameter guesses or bounds, `curvefit` should still infer defaults and preserve prior scalar behavior for the unspecified parameters.
When fitting fails for a slice and `errors` is left as `"raise"`, the operation should raise rather than returning a partial success result.
When fitting fails for a slice and `errors="ignore"` is used, the returned coefficient and covariance outputs for that slice should be `NaN` while other slices can still be returned normally.
When the caller passes an unsupported `errors` value, `curvefit` should reject it with `ValueError`.

task_2.title: Support partial curve fitting failures and dimension-aware fit inputs
task_2.description: The upgrade extends xarray curve fitting so batch fits can continue when some slices fail, returning NaN results for failed fits when requested, and allows parameter guesses and bounds to vary across preserved dimensions through DataArray inputs.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that batch uses of `curvefit` can optionally tolerate individual optimization failures without aborting the entire operation, while also supporting per-slice initial guesses and bounds that align with the non-reduced dimensions of the data.

expectation.grounded: `Dataset.curvefit()` and `DataArray.curvefit()` must accept an `errors` option with `"raise"` and `"ignore"`. With `errors="raise"`, optimization failures from SciPy fitting continue to surface as exceptions. With `errors="ignore"`, failed fits must produce NaN values in both the returned coefficient array and covariance array for the affected coordinates while successful fits remain available. The `p0` argument may accept floats or `DataArray` values, and `bounds` may accept tuples whose lower and upper entries are floats or `DataArray` values, with DataArray inputs broadcast across preserved dimensions.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to run curve fitting across many series without losing all results because a subset of fits fails. They should also be able to provide different starting guesses or bounds for different slices of the data, as long as those inputs align with the dimensions being preserved in the output.

constraints.grounded: Only `errors="raise"` and `errors="ignore"` are valid. `DataArray` values supplied through `p0` or `bounds` must not introduce dimensions outside the dimensions preserved by the fit; invalid dimensionality must be rejected with `ValueError`. Existing behavior for successful fits, skipped-NaN handling, and default parameter and bound inference must remain intact.
constraints.conceptual: The new flexibility must not change the outcome of successful fits or silently accept misaligned inputs. Invalid mode values or per-slice fit inputs that do not match the output grouping should fail clearly rather than being guessed or reshaped implicitly.

behavior: Batch curve fitting can return partial results when some individual fits fail, instead of aborting the full operation.
When failure tolerance is enabled, failed fits yield NaN parameter estimates and NaN covariance values at the corresponding output positions.
When failure tolerance is not enabled, fitting failures still raise an exception.
Initial parameter guesses can vary by preserved dimensions through `DataArray` inputs to `p0`.
Lower and upper parameter bounds can vary by preserved dimensions through `DataArray` inputs to `bounds`, including mixed scalar and array bounds.
Per-slice guesses or bounds with unexpected dimensions are rejected before fitting.
These behaviors apply consistently for eager and dask-backed curve fitting.
acceptance_criteria: When `DataArray.curvefit()` or `Dataset.curvefit()` is run over multiple series and one series fails to converge, using `errors="ignore"` should return fitted results for successful series and NaN coefficients and covariances for the failed series.
When the same failing fit is run with the default error mode, it should raise the optimization exception instead of returning partial results.
When `p0` is provided as `DataArray` values aligned to preserved dimensions, each slice should be fit using its own broadcasted initial guess.
When `bounds` is provided with `DataArray` lower and/or upper bounds aligned to preserved dimensions, each slice should respect its own broadcasted bounds.
When a `p0` or `bounds` `DataArray` contains dimensions that are not preserved by the fit, the call should fail with `ValueError`.
When an unsupported `errors` value is supplied, the call should fail with `ValueError`.
When all fits succeed, enabling the new options should not change the fitted values apart from the intended per-slice guesses or bounds.

task_3.title: Deprecate DataArray cdms2 conversion methods
task_3.description: The upgrade deprecates xarray DataArray conversion entry points that depend on the retired cdms2 ecosystem. Existing cdms2 conversions still run, but calling them now surfaces deprecation warnings so users can migrate away from cdms2-compatible workflows.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray users who convert DataArray objects to or from cdms2 are clearly informed that this interoperability path is deprecated and should be treated as legacy behavior while remaining usable during the transition period.

expectation.grounded: Calling `DataArray.to_cdms2()` or `DataArray.from_cdms2()` in xarray 2023.6.0 should continue performing the conversion, but each call should emit a `DeprecationWarning` indicating that the `cdms2`-based conversion path is deprecated and that users should consider an alternative library. The deprecation is part of the documented public API status for these methods in 2023.6.0.
expectation.conceptual: The upgrade should preserve existing cdms2 conversion behavior for now, but any user invoking those conversions should receive a clear deprecation signal at call time so they can migrate off the deprecated interoperability path.

constraints.grounded: The deprecation must not remove or silently alter the observable conversion results of `DataArray.to_cdms2()` and `DataArray.from_cdms2()` for supported environments; successful conversions should still round-trip data, dimensions, names, and relevant coordinates as before. The only new runtime signal is the deprecation warning. Compatibility expectations are limited because `cdms2` is unmaintained and tests are not expected to run on newer Python or NumPy combinations unsupported by `cdms2`.
constraints.conceptual: Users should still be able to use the legacy conversion workflow where their environment supports it, with no regression in returned data or metadata beyond the addition of a deprecation warning. The upgrade does not promise continued compatibility for unsupported modern dependency combinations.

behavior: Invoking `DataArray.to_cdms2()` emits a `DeprecationWarning` and still returns a cdms2 variable representation.
Invoking `DataArray.from_cdms2()` emits a `DeprecationWarning` and still returns an xarray `DataArray`.
Existing cdms2 round-trip behavior remains intact for supported classic, structured-grid, and unstructured-grid conversion scenarios.
The deprecation is user-visible both in runtime warning behavior and in the API documentation status of the affected methods.
The cdms2 interoperability path is treated as legacy because upstream `cdms2` support is no longer expected to keep pace with newer Python and NumPy versions.
acceptance_criteria: When a user calls `DataArray.to_cdms2()` in a supported environment, it should emit a `DeprecationWarning` and still produce a cdms2 object representing the original data and metadata.
When a user calls `DataArray.from_cdms2()` in a supported environment, it should emit a `DeprecationWarning` and still reconstruct an equivalent `DataArray` from the cdms2 input.
When a `DataArray` is converted to cdms2 and back in supported classic or grid-based cases, the resulting xarray object should preserve the original data values, dimensions, coordinates, and name.
When users upgrade to 2023.6.0, they should be able to detect from the public API behavior that cdms2 conversion methods are deprecated rather than fully removed.
When running under environments not supported by the unmaintained cdms2 stack, the upgrade should not be interpreted as restoring compatibility guarantees for those newer dependency versions.

task_4.title: Improve concat scalability for large datasets
task_4.description: The update improves the performance of xarray dataset concatenation and related coordinate-based combination workflows for large inputs, especially when concatenating along large dimensions or when some variables are missing from some datasets. The change is intended to reduce overhead without changing the observable concat and combine contracts around dimension alignment, coordinate presence, index consistency, and reindexing behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that concatenating or combining large datasets remains responsive and scales to large concat dimensions without changing the user-visible results, validation behavior, or handling of partially present variables.

expectation.grounded: In xarray 2023.6.0, dataset concatenation and related combination flows, including concat()-driven dataset assembly and combine_by_coords(), should handle large concat dimensions more efficiently while preserving the existing observable behavior of Variable.concat and dataset concatenation. Concatenated outputs must still preserve dimension ordering, support concatenation along an existing dimension or stacking along a new dimension, reindex variables that are absent from some datasets, and continue to raise ValueError when a required coordinate is missing from one or more datasets or when a variable's index presence is inconsistent across datasets.
expectation.conceptual: Upgrading should make large concatenation workloads noticeably faster while keeping the same results and failure modes that users already rely on. Combining datasets should still produce the same merged structure, preserve coordinate alignment, and reject invalid inputs in the same user-visible situations.

constraints.grounded: The update must not change the public concat/combine semantics for valid inputs: concatenated variables must retain the expected dimensions and ordering, missing non-coordinate variables must still be expanded through reindexing across the concat dimension, coordinate variables must still be required across all datasets when needed, and mixed presence of indexes for the same variable across datasets must still be rejected. Dimension compatibility checks across concatenated variables must continue to be enforced.
constraints.conceptual: Performance gains must not come at the cost of correctness. Existing successful concatenations should keep producing equivalent outputs, and existing invalid cases should still fail instead of silently changing structure or alignment.

behavior: Concatenating datasets along very large dimensions should complete with lower overhead than before.
Combining datasets by coordinates should benefit from the same scalability improvements when it relies on concatenation internally.
When a non-coordinate variable is present in only a subset of datasets, the combined result should still be reindexed so the variable aligns correctly across the full concatenation axis.
When a coordinate required for concatenation is missing from any dataset, the operation should still fail with a ValueError.
When the same variable has an index in only some of the input datasets, the operation should still fail with a ValueError.
Concatenation should continue to preserve whether the target dimension already exists on the input variables or must be introduced as a new leading dimension.
acceptance_criteria: When concatenating datasets with very large concat dimensions, the operation should return the same logical result as before while exhibiting improved runtime characteristics.
When combine_by_coords() is used on large compatible datasets, it should produce the expected merged dataset without behavioral regressions in variable or coordinate alignment.

Given a variable that is missing from some datasets but is not a required coordinate, when datasets are concatenated, the result should still include that variable aligned to the full concat dimension via reindexing.
Given a required coordinate that is absent from one of the input datasets, when concatenation is attempted, it should raise ValueError.
Given a variable that has an index in some input datasets and no index in others, when concatenation is attempted, it should raise ValueError.
Given input variables with incompatible dimension layouts outside the concat dimension, when concatenation is attempted, it should continue to reject the input rather than silently reshaping it.

task_5.title: Prevent weighted polyfit from mutating source xarray objects
task_5.description: Upgrading to 2023.6.0 fixes a bug where calling weighted polynomial fitting could overwrite the data in the original xarray object. After the update, weighted polyfit preserves the input object while still producing the fit result.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that running weighted polynomial fitting does not modify the original data being fit, and that users can call polyfit with weights without their source xarray object being overwritten or corrupted.

expectation.grounded: Calling `polyfit(..., w=...)` on an xarray object must leave the original object unchanged. This non-mutation guarantee must hold for weighted fits in the same way it already does for unweighted fits, with the fit result returned separately and the source object remaining identical before and after the call.
expectation.conceptual: Weighted polynomial fitting should behave like a read-only analytical operation. Supplying weights may affect the fit result, but it must not alter the input data, coordinates, or overall source object state.

constraints.grounded: The fix must preserve existing `polyfit` behavior aside from eliminating in-place mutation of the input when `w` is provided. Weighted and unweighted calls must continue to return fit outputs normally, and the original xarray object must remain identical after a weighted call.
constraints.conceptual: The update should remove the side effect without changing the intended fitting workflow. Users should not need defensive copies just to protect their original data during weighted fitting.

behavior: A weighted `polyfit` call no longer overwrites values in the source xarray object.
Providing `w` changes only the computed fit result, not the caller-owned input data.
After weighted fitting completes, the original object should compare as unchanged relative to its pre-call state.
The mutation bug affected weighted fitting specifically; unweighted fitting semantics remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When a user calls `polyfit` without weights, it should continue to leave the original object unchanged.
When a user calls `polyfit` with `w` provided, it should return the fit result without modifying the original object.
Given an xarray object copied before a weighted `polyfit` call, the original object should remain identical to the copy after the call.
When weights are used, the only observable effect should be on the fitting output, not on the stored source data.

task_6.title: Avoid shutdown-time file manager errors in script-based dataset workflows
task_6.description: The upgrade fixes a shutdown-time bug in xarray's cached file handling so script-driven multi-file dataset workflows no longer emit interpreter-exit errors after otherwise successful I/O operations. This improves reliability for users opening multiple NetCDF files and writing combined outputs in non-interactive execution.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that script-based dataset aggregation and export workflows complete without shutdown-time errors when cached backend files remain managed by xarray at interpreter exit.

expectation.grounded: When users run workflows involving xarray backend file caching, including opening multiple files through APIs such as `xr.open_mfdataset(...)` and then writing results, `CachingFileManager` must not raise interpreter-shutdown exceptions from its destructor path during process teardown. The library should avoid relying on `CachingFileManager.__del__` once Python exit handling begins.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to run dataset loading and export code as a normal script and have the process exit cleanly. Successful reads and writes should not be followed by spurious cleanup errors just because the interpreter is shutting down.

constraints.grounded: Normal runtime file-manager behavior must remain unchanged while the process is active. The fix must only suppress destructor-based cleanup during interpreter exit and must not alter the public dataset-loading or writing APIs, expected successful output generation, or ordinary non-shutdown error behavior.
constraints.conceptual: The change should only remove false-positive shutdown noise, not weaken normal runtime behavior or change how users call the library. Existing successful workflows should keep working the same way aside from cleaner process termination.

behavior: Script executions that use cached xarray backend files should no longer emit `TypeError`-style exceptions during interpreter shutdown after completing work.
Workflows that open multiple NetCDF files and serialize combined results should terminate cleanly in non-interactive contexts.
Destructor-based cleanup for cached file managers is disabled at interpreter exit rather than being invoked after Python has begun tearing down global state.
Observable runtime behavior before interpreter shutdown, including dataset access and file output, remains unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When a user opens multiple files with xarray and writes a combined output in a standalone script, the script should finish without shutdown-time exceptions after the output is produced.
When the same workflow is run interactively or non-interactively, successful operations should not differ in whether interpreter-exit cleanup errors are emitted.
When xarray backend file managers still exist at process teardown, interpreter shutdown should not trigger destructor-related failures.
When normal dataset loading or writing fails for unrelated reasons, the library should still surface those runtime errors as usual.

task_7.title: Preserve empty variable-length string dtypes across backend roundtrips
task_7.description: The update fixes a data roundtrip issue where empty arrays intended to represent variable-length strings could be reloaded with a numeric dtype instead of preserving string semantics. Version 2023.6.0 keeps variable-length string dtype metadata intact through CF encoding and supported backend reads so empty and non-empty string arrays behave consistently.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that empty arrays representing variable-length strings retain their string dtype semantics when encoded, saved, and reopened, so users do not observe dtype changes during dataset roundtrips.

expectation.grounded: Datasets and variables using variable-length string object dtypes, including dtypes created with xarray string-coding helpers and equivalent backend metadata, should preserve that dtype through CF encoding and backend roundtrips. Reading from supported backends should surface the array as object dtype with variable-length string metadata instead of coercing empty arrays to float64 or stripping the string marker.
expectation.conceptual: When a dataset contains an empty string-like array, saving and reopening it should still behave like a string array rather than changing into a numeric array. Empty and non-empty variable-length string arrays should be treated consistently.

constraints.grounded: The fix should apply only to object dtypes that are explicitly marked as variable-length strings. Existing handling for other object arrays must remain unchanged, and backends that cannot roundtrip dtype metadata may still return plain object dtype as long as they do not misclassify the data as numeric.
constraints.conceptual: The change must be narrowly scoped to genuine string arrays and must not alter unrelated object-array behavior. Systems with limited metadata support should degrade safely without inventing the wrong dtype.

behavior: Empty variable-length string arrays preserve string dtype semantics during dataset roundtrip operations.
CF encoding leaves variable-length string object dtypes unchanged instead of coercing them through generic object-dtype conversion paths.
Backend readers recognize variable-length string metadata from xarray-managed and compatible backend-specific representations.
Supported backends return reopened empty string arrays as object dtype carrying variable-length string meaning, rather than converting them to float64.
acceptance_criteria: When a dataset variable is an empty variable-length string array and the dataset is written and reopened with a metadata-capable backend, it should remain equal to the original and preserve variable-length string dtype semantics.
When a dataset variable is a non-empty variable-length string array, encoding and roundtrip behavior should continue to preserve its string dtype semantics.
When CF encoding is applied to a variable-length string object array, it should keep string dtype metadata rather than treating the value as a generic object array.
When a backend exposes compatible variable-length string metadata, xarray should recognize it as a string dtype on read.
When an object array is not marked as a variable-length string, existing object-dtype handling should remain unchanged.

task_8.title: Preserve DataArray dtype when reindexing empty arrays
task_8.description: The update fixes a user-visible dtype regression in xarray where reindexing an empty DataArray could change its dtype during missing-value filling. In 2023.6.0, reindex preserves the original array dtype, including float32, so empty-array reindex results behave consistently with non-empty arrays.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that reindexing an empty DataArray preserves the original dtype instead of widening it during alignment and missing-value handling.

expectation.grounded: In xarray 2023.6.0, DataArray.reindex() should return a DataArray whose dtype matches the source DataArray dtype even when the source is empty and reindex introduces missing positions. For a float32 DataArray, the reindexed result should remain float32 rather than being promoted to float64.
expectation.conceptual: Reindexing should not unexpectedly change the data type of a DataArray just because the array is empty or because the operation creates missing entries. Users should observe dtype stability before and after reindex.

constraints.grounded: The dtype-preservation behavior must hold for empty DataArray inputs passed through DataArray.reindex(), and it must remain consistent with existing reindex behavior for non-empty arrays. Missing-value support used during reindex must not force an avoidable dtype widening when the original dtype can represent the result.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to preserving observable data types during reindex and must not introduce regressions in normal reindex results or in how missing values are represented for supported dtypes.

behavior: Calling DataArray.reindex() on an empty DataArray preserves the source dtype in the returned DataArray.
When an empty float32 DataArray is reindexed to new coordinate labels, the result remains float32.
The dtype of a reindex result is expected to match the original DataArray dtype rather than being widened solely because fill values are inserted.
acceptance_criteria: When an empty DataArray with dtype float32 is reindexed to coordinates that add new positions, the returned DataArray should have dtype float32.
When comparing the source DataArray dtype and the reindexed DataArray dtype for an empty input, they should be equal.

When reindex is applied to empty inputs, dtype preservation should be consistent with the existing expectation that non-empty reindex operations retain the original dtype when no incompatible type conversion is required.

task_9.title: Honor explicit empty Zarr chunk_store values
task_9.description: The update fixes Zarr writing so that an explicitly provided empty chunk store is used during `to_zarr` operations instead of being ignored as though no chunk store had been supplied. This restores the expected separation of metadata and chunk data storage for valid empty store instances.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that writing data with `to_zarr(..., chunk_store=...)` uses an explicitly provided Zarr chunk store even when that store is currently empty, rather than treating the empty store as absent.

expectation.grounded: When a caller passes a non-`None` `chunk_store` to the Zarr backend, including a zero-length store object that implements `__len__`, the backend should forward that store to the write/open configuration exactly as the provided chunk store. The presence check must distinguish `None` from an empty store so chunk data is written to the supplied `chunk_store`, and datasets remain readable when that same `chunk_store` is supplied through backend kwargs.
expectation.conceptual: Providing a chunk store should depend on whether the caller supplied one, not on whether it already contains data. Empty-but-valid chunk stores must behave the same as pre-populated ones: they receive chunk data during write and can be used to read the dataset afterward.

constraints.grounded: Only a `None` `chunk_store` should be treated as missing. Empty stores, falsey store objects, and stores whose length is zero must still be honored if explicitly passed. Existing behavior for omitted `chunk_store` values and successful round-trip reading with a provided chunk store must remain intact.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not change behavior for callers who do not provide a chunk store. It should only correct the falsey-empty-store case and preserve normal read/write compatibility for valid chunk-store configurations.

behavior: An explicitly supplied empty Zarr `chunk_store` is now used during write operations instead of being ignored.
Chunk-store handling now distinguishes between `None` and other falsey store objects.
After writing with an initially empty `chunk_store`, the chunk store becomes populated with chunk entries.
A dataset written with a supplied `chunk_store` remains readable when that same chunk store is provided on open.
acceptance_criteria: When `to_zarr` is called with a valid empty `chunk_store`, it should write chunk data into that store rather than behaving as if no chunk store was provided.
When the provided `chunk_store` has length zero before the write, it should contain stored chunk entries after the write completes.
When a dataset is reopened with backend configuration that includes the same `chunk_store`, the loaded dataset should match the data that was written.
When `chunk_store=None` or the argument is omitted, behavior should remain consistent with existing no-chunk-store handling.

task_10.title: Improve Array API astype compatibility
task_10.description: The update improves compatibility with Python Array API compliant arrays by ensuring xarray uses standard-compliant dtype conversion paths in string-processing and variable-padding/fill operations, reducing failures when arrays do not expose a non-standard instance-level astype method.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray operations continue to work with Python Array API compliant array backends when dtype conversion is required, especially for string accessor operations and padding or missing-value handling paths that previously depended on non-standard array methods.

expectation.grounded: xarray should perform dtype conversion through its array-API-compatible casting path rather than relying on an array object's own `.astype()` method. This applies to `StringAccessor` operations that reshape string results, including extraction, partitioning, and splitting behaviors, and to `Variable` paths involved in padding and NA-based fill handling. For supported inputs, these operations should return the same shaped results and dtype-kind-preserving outputs as before while remaining compatible with arrays that only implement the Array API casting interface.
expectation.conceptual: When xarray needs to change an array's dtype internally, that conversion should use a standards-compliant mechanism so the same user-facing operations work across NumPy and other Array API compatible backends. Users should observe successful execution and unchanged high-level results rather than backend-specific casting failures.

constraints.grounded: Existing observable semantics must remain stable: string accessor methods should still preserve the expected string/object result kind, padding-related operations should still honor requested fill values and pad modes, and NA-promotion flows should still promote dtype only when required. The change must not introduce new public APIs or alter the returned dimensional structure of existing operations.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should expand backend compatibility without changing the meaning of existing features. Results, shapes, and dtype behavior should stay consistent with prior releases except that previously failing standards-compliant backends should now work.

behavior: String accessor operations that internally cast intermediate object arrays back to the source string-kind result should succeed on Array API compliant backends without requiring an instance `.astype()` implementation.
Padding flows that require casting to a promoted or fill-compatible dtype should use a backend-compatible casting path before applying padding.
Missing-value handling paths that promote dtype for NA support should cast through the same compatible mechanism instead of backend-specific array methods.
Observable outputs should remain consistent in shape and dtype intent with prior behavior for backends that already worked.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs affected string accessor operations on data backed by an Array API compliant array library, the operation should complete without failing due to a missing instance-level `.astype()` method.
When extraction, partitioning, or splitting operations produce string-like results, they should preserve the expected result kind and output dimensionality.
When padding requires dtype conversion to apply a fill value, the padded result should still respect the requested pad behavior and fill semantics.
When filling with missing values requires dtype promotion, the result should still promote dtype as needed and complete successfully on compatible backends.
When the same operations are run on previously supported backends such as NumPy, their user-visible behavior should remain unchanged.

task_11.title: Publish nightly wheels to the Scientific Python nightly index
task_11.description: The 2023.6.0 update adds distribution support for xarray nightly wheel builds so downstream projects can install prebuilt development snapshots from the Scientific Python nightly wheel index and test against unreleased dependency versions more easily.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that development snapshots of the library are published as nightly wheels to the Scientific Python nightly package index so downstream users and integrators can install and test unreleased builds without building from source.

expectation.grounded: The project should publish nightly wheel artifacts for xarray to the Scientific Python nightly wheels index at the documented Anaconda package source. The upgrade should expose nightly installability for development builds and support downstream CI workflows that test against developer versions of dependencies. No public runtime API additions, removals, or changed error semantics are evidenced by the provided materials.
expectation.conceptual: Users who rely on pre-release integration testing should be able to install a nightly build of the library from the shared Scientific Python nightly package repository and use it in dependency compatibility testing the same way they use other ecosystem nightly packages. Existing library behavior at runtime should remain unchanged.

constraints.grounded: The change should be limited to nightly wheel distribution and must not introduce observable changes to xarray's public Python API, data model behavior, warning behavior, or exception behavior based on the provided evidence. Stable release installation paths should remain unaffected.
constraints.conceptual: This update should only expand how unreleased builds are distributed. Regular users on standard releases should see no functional behavior changes, and nightly availability should not degrade normal installation or usage expectations.

behavior: Nightly wheel artifacts are made available from the Scientific Python nightly wheels package index.
Downstream projects can consume nightly builds as prebuilt packages for CI or compatibility testing against development dependency stacks.
The upgrade reflects packaging and release-process support rather than a new end-user runtime feature.
No user-visible runtime API or semantic change is evidenced in the supplied diff materials.
acceptance_criteria: When a downstream maintainer configures installation from the Scientific Python nightly wheels index, they should be able to resolve and install a nightly xarray wheel without building from source.
When teams test against developer versions of Scientific Python dependencies, they should be able to include xarray nightly builds in the same workflow.
When existing users install normal released versions through standard channels, the upgrade should not require any changes to their runtime usage of the library.
When reviewing the upgrade from a product perspective, it should be classified as a distribution and ecosystem integration improvement rather than a runtime API feature.

task_12.title: Retire TestPyPI development wheel publishing
task_12.description: Version 2023.6.0 stops publishing development wheels to TestPyPI because nightly wheel distribution is handled through a different channel. The change affects how pre-release artifacts are distributed, not the runtime behavior of the library itself.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 2023.6.0 no longer relies on TestPyPI as a source for development or nightly wheel builds, and that users understand nightly or pre-release distributions are provided through the supported replacement channel instead.

expectation.grounded: In 2023.6.0, development-wheel publishing to TestPyPI is retired. Consumers of pre-release distribution artifacts should not expect new xarray development wheels to appear on TestPyPI after this upgrade, and existing workflows that discover nightly builds from TestPyPI are no longer supported by the project release process.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, pre-release package discovery should follow the project’s supported nightly distribution path rather than TestPyPI. Regular library usage should remain unchanged, but users who consume nightly builds need to adjust to the new distribution source.

constraints.grounded: Do not treat this upgrade as introducing public API, runtime, or behavioral changes in xarray itself without additional evidence. Preserve standard installation and execution behavior for stable releases, and scope the change to availability of development-wheel artifacts on TestPyPI.
constraints.conceptual: This change should only affect where pre-release packages are obtained. It should not be interpreted as changing normal library features, semantics, or stable-install behavior.

behavior: New development or nightly wheel uploads are no longer published to TestPyPI.
Users depending on TestPyPI for pre-release xarray artifacts must switch to the supported nightly distribution channel.
Stable runtime behavior of the installed library is not changed by this release-note item alone.
acceptance_criteria: When a user looks for new 2023.6.0-era development wheels on TestPyPI, they should not expect them to be published there.
When a user consumes nightly or pre-release builds, they should be directed to the supported replacement distribution channel rather than TestPyPI.
When a user installs or runs stable releases, the upgrade should not imply any observable runtime API change from this item alone.

task_13.title: Handle optional import name collisions during duck typing
task_13.description: The upgrade makes optional duck-array dependency detection more tolerant of package name collisions. When a module imported for duck typing exists under the expected name but does not expose the expected API and raises an AttributeError during inspection, the library now treats it as unavailable instead of failing import-time compatibility checks.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that optional duck-typed dependency detection does not fail when an installed package shares the expected import name but does not implement the expected interface. Ensure that environments with such package collisions continue to operate by falling back as if the optional dependency were unavailable.

expectation.grounded: During duck typing in `xarray.core.pycompat`, optional dependency probing for a duck array module must treat both `ImportError` and `AttributeError` as signals that the target integration is unavailable. If importing or inspecting a candidate module such as `pint` raises `AttributeError` because the imported package is a different distribution with the same import name, `DuckArrayModule` should resolve to no available module, version `0.0.0`, and an empty type tuple rather than propagating the exception.
expectation.conceptual: Optional compatibility checks should be resilient to package name collisions. If a similarly named installed package does not provide the expected API and triggers an attribute-based failure during detection, the library should behave as though the optional dependency is not installed and continue running without crashing.

constraints.grounded: Valid optional integrations that import and expose the expected attributes must continue to be recognized normally. Only `ImportError` and `AttributeError` raised during duck-array module detection are newly tolerated; successful imports must keep their existing behavior, and unrelated exception handling should not be broadened beyond these observable failure modes.
constraints.conceptual: The change must reduce false failures from dependency discovery without masking normal successful integrations or changing behavior for correctly installed supported packages. It should only soften clearly dependency-detection-related import and attribute lookup failures.

behavior: Duck-typed optional dependency detection now falls back cleanly when module inspection raises `AttributeError`.
Package name collisions that import a different library under an expected module name are treated as an unavailable optional dependency instead of a hard failure.
When fallback occurs, the detected module state remains empty and non-active rather than partially initialized.
Normal detection of correctly installed optional dependencies is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When an environment contains a package under an expected optional dependency import name but that package lacks the required attributes and raises `AttributeError` during detection, the library should not raise and should continue as if that optional dependency is unavailable.
When the expected optional dependency is genuinely missing and raises `ImportError`, the library should continue using the existing unavailable-dependency fallback behavior.
When the correct optional dependency is installed and exposes the expected interface, duck typing should still recognize it successfully.
When fallback is triggered by import or attribute lookup failure, observable compatibility state should indicate no active duck-array module support rather than a partially detected module.
